DOI:10.1136/heartjnl-2013-305296.topic: Secondary prevention after acute coronary syndrome
DOI:10.1136/heartjnl-2013-305296.setting: All hospitals admitting ACS patients in Australia and New Zealand; bi-national prospective audit
DOI:10.1136/heartjnl-2013-305296.standard: Optimal in-hospital preventive care: lifestyle advice, referral to rehabilitation and prescription of secondary prevention pharmacotherapies

cycle1.result: 46% referred to rehabilitation; 65% discharged on sufficient preventive medications; 27% received optimal preventive care.

DOI:10.1136/heartjnl-2013-305296.other_findings: STEMI (OR 2.64), NSTEMI (OR 1.99), PCI (OR 4.71), CABG (OR 2.10) and hypertension were associated with more preventive care; age over 70 (OR 0.53) and private hospital admission (OR 0.59) with less.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.453.setting: Surrey and Borders Partnership NHS Trust; patients presented at Personality Disorder forums
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.453.standard: NICE guidance on drug treatment in borderline personality disorder; two audit standards and four treatment targets from the POMH-UK audit; Trust 'Guidance for Prescribing in Personality Disorder' (Dec 2020)

cycle1.result: Crisis plan documented 87%; clinical reason for antipsychotic documented 43%; antipsychotics >4 weeks without psychosis 86%; Z-hypnotics >4 weeks 13%; benzodiazepines >4 weeks 28%; medication reviews 90%.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.453.intervention: Trust 'Guidance for Prescribing in Personality Disorder' published and circulated across the Trust in December 2020.

cycle2.result: Crisis plan documented 79%; clinical reason for antipsychotic documented 69%; antipsychotics >4 weeks without psychosis 91%; Z-hypnotics >4 weeks 37.5%; benzodiazepines >4 weeks 38%; medication reviews 100% of eligible patients.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.453.other_findings: Quality of medication reviews remained similar to 2017; POMH-UK national audits were done in 2012 and 2014. Findings to be presented with re-emphasis on guidelines and re-audit in 2 years.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10588.topic: Did not attend follow-up actions in outpatient clinics
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10588.setting: Learning disability outpatient mental health service, BCHFT
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10588.standard: Trust DNA policy: ring patient after DNA, check awareness of appointment, discuss barriers and document

cycle1.result: 35/117 (29%) appointments were DNA. Staff telephoned 34% after the DNA but no policy-aligned details were documented; no contact for 57%; no documentation for 9%. 83% offered another appointment, 17% discharged to GP.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10588.other_findings: DNA was associated with male gender, living with family and neuropsychiatric comorbidity. Recommendations: adapt DNA policy for this group and raise awareness at induction.

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znad348.079.setting: Acute general surgery department, University Hospital Hairmyres, East Kilbride; single centre retrospective audit
DOI:10.1093/bjs/znad348.079.standard: Surviving Sepsis Campaign 2021: lactate measured within 3 hours of admission and repeated within 4–6 hours if ≥2 mmol

cycle1.result: Surgical ward: lactate repeated in 16 (28.6%) patients with high lactate, 9 (56%) of these at ≥8 hours. HDU/ICU: 12 (92%) had lactate repeated in the target time.

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znad348.079.other_findings: Standards were not achieved on the ward, attributed to unawareness of recommendations and time pressure.

DOI:10.1136/bmjoq-2022-002096.setting: AIC Kijabe Hospital, tertiary training hospital

cycle1.result: not reported

DOI:10.1136/bmjoq-2022-002096.other_findings: Describes a five-category mortality classification system for low-resource settings used to drive trainee, departmental and system learning.

DOI:10.1093/bjd/ljag086.297.topic: JAK inhibitor prescribing for alopecia areata
DOI:10.1093/bjd/ljag086.297.setting: Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board, North Wales; regional retrospective audit
DOI:10.1093/bjd/ljag086.297.standard: BAD guidance on ritlecitinib: eligibility, safety screening, outcome monitoring and psychological support

cycle1.result: Baseline SALT ≥50 in 94% (n=16); psychological screening documented 65% (n=11); referred for psychological support 29% (n=5); wig services 82% (n=14); counselling on long-term treatment 47% (n=8); pharmacovigilance registry enrolment 0%.

DOI:10.1093/bjd/ljag086.297.other_findings: At 36 weeks 12% (n=2) achieved SALT ≤20; 5 (29%) did not reach week 36. A standardised regional pathway was recommended.

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znag087.373.setting: Two acute hospitals in one UK health board (NHS Lanarkshire); biliary stone pathway database
DOI:10.1093/bjs/znag087.373.standard: UK legal and professional (GMC) standards: documentation of material risks and reasonable alternatives (options-based shared decision-making) before ERCP

cycle1.result: Options-based SDM documented in 73/356 (20.5%) ERCP episodes: low risk 19/78 (24.4%), medium 21/141 (14.9%), high 33/137 (24.1%) (p=0.105). Increased from 12.5% (2023Q4) to 31.8% (2024Q4) (p=0.160). LCBDE 38/38 (100%).

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znag087.373.other_findings: ERCP 30- and 90-day mortality 1.4% (5/355) and 2.5% (9/355). An options-led consent template was proposed.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.489.topic: Shared care transfer of antipsychotic depot prescribing
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.489.setting: Rochdale, Heywood and Middleton community mental health team depot clinics
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.489.standard: GMMMG Shared Care Pathway: prescribing of depots for stable patients transferred to GP; target 100%

cycle1.result: Overall compliance 83%.

cycle2.result: Overall compliance 96%; first generation antipsychotics 98%; paliperidone and risperidone 94%; aripiprazole 91%.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.489.other_findings: One team was 99% compliant overall. The 100% target was still not met; transfers between teams were a weak point.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10679.topic: Mental health admissions to paediatric assessment unit
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10679.setting: Paediatric Assessment Unit, Royal Aberdeen Children's Hospital

cycle1.result: 98/4898 (2%) PAU admissions were for mental health; 87% received a psychiatry review; mean stay 2.1 days (1–20).

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10679.other_findings: 27% needed treatment for paracetamol overdose and 7% for anorexia; 75% followed up by CAMHS, 22% had no follow-up.

DOI:10.1136/heartjnl-2016-309706.topic: Heart failure discharge key performance measures
DOI:10.1136/heartjnl-2016-309706.setting: 185 hospitals in England and Wales; National Heart Failure Audit
DOI:10.1136/heartjnl-2016-309706.standard: Three key performance measures: ACE-I/ARB on discharge, beta-blocker on discharge, referral to specialist follow-up

cycle1.result: Composite KPM adherence by hospital ranged 50% to 97% (median 79%); referral to specialist follow-up median 81% (range 20% to 100%).

DOI:10.1136/heartjnl-2016-309706.other_findings: Only 8% of composite variation (7% ACE-I/ARB, 6% beta-blocker) was attributable to hospital features, versus 26% for specialist referral.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afae178.171.setting: 11 specialist Parkinson's disease services (geriatrician- or neurologist-led); national audit
DOI:10.1093/ageing/afae178.171.standard: De novo audit tool based on international standards, guidelines and audit tools

cycle1.result: 16.8% seen less than annually; motor and mobility assessment >75%; cognition 70%; pain 64%; saliva management 50%; bone density 18%; PD nurse access 65%; physiotherapy 69%; SLT 53%; OT 50%; written information after diagnosis 24%.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afae178.171.other_findings: Geriatric-led services screened more for malnutrition (99% v 78%) and orthostatic hypotension (94% v 52%). Carer communication poorly documented (financial support 12%).

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.904.topic: Mental Health Act consent to treatment documentation
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.904.setting: Adult acute and rehab wards, Roseberry Park Hospital
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.904.standard: MHA documentation for section 3 patients staying 90 days or more: MCA1 capacity assessment at admission and 3 months, T2 form, SOAD request and T3 authorisation

cycle1.result: Capacity assessment documented 80% at admission and 60% at 3 months; T2 completed in all consenting patients; SOAD request sent in 7 (78%) but recorded in 5 (56%); T3 documented in 4 (45%), discussed with patient in 1 (11%).

cycle2.result: Capacity assessment 80% at admission and 60% at 3 months; T2 completed in all consenting patients; SOAD request recorded in 1 (25%); T3 not documented or discussed for any patient.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.904.other_findings: Rehab ward closed in February 2020 so re-audit covered acute wards only. No change between cycles was described.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.248.topic: Crisis safety plans for high intensity users
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.248.setting: Acute mental health services (s136 suite, liaison and inpatient wards)
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.248.standard: Safety plan in place containing person-centred, specific recommendations to avert and manage crisis

cycle1.result: >80% had a safety plan, but these lacked sufficient detail to avert crisis or guide treatment.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.248.intervention: HIU response plan template, best practice example for care coordinators and process for flagging HIUs to community teams, developed through process mapping, driver diagram and focus groups.

cycle2.result: HIU response plans incorporated into the safety plans of 20/26 HIUs.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.248.other_findings: Most frequent diagnosis was EUPD (77%); 93% on CPA. PDSA cycles ongoing.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.523.topic: Management of behavioural symptoms in dementia
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.523.setting: Humber Older People's Mental Health Services
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.523.standard: NICE: non-pharmacological before pharmacological management; antipsychotics started low and slow; follow-up at least 6 weeks after starting

cycle1.result: About 24% started on medication without trial of non-pharmacological methods; those started on medication were properly followed up; overall adherence around 75%.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.523.other_findings: Risperidone was the commonest medication (37%). Re-audit suggested in 12 to 24 months.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afz103.88.setting: General medical ward and specialist geriatric medicine ward, city centre teaching hospital (Mercy University Hospital, Cork)
DOI:10.1093/ageing/afz103.88.standard: Audit tool adapted from the RCP National Continence Audit tool and the hospital elimination documentation pathway

cycle1.result: 4 patients had no continence status documented; of over-65s with documented incontinence (42%), only 40% had the nursing elimination section fully completed; 6 had symptoms/type documented; catheter indications documented in both catheterised patients.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afz103.88.other_findings: An assessment tool and education programme were planned for the geriatric ward.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afab219.26.setting: 30-bed independent care home intermediate care unit with NHS trust MDT (SEHSCT, Dundonald)

cycle1.result: Baseline nursing confidence in handover assessed by semi-structured interviews and weighted questionnaire.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afab219.26.intervention: Care-home-specific electronic nursing handover template based on National Audit of Intermediate Care quality indicators, four iterations.

cycle2.result: 70% reported increased or slightly increased confidence in addressing questions from residents or relatives, responding to change in health status and giving handover.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afab219.26.other_findings: Measured staff confidence rather than compliance with a standard.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.612.setting: Memory clinic, Stockton Mental Health Services for Older People
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.612.standard: Trust and NICE standards: minimum body of key information recorded in electronic records within 24 hours of diagnostic assessment

cycle1.result: Minimum body of information recorded in 90–100% of cases.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.612.intervention: All diagnosing clinicians informed about the project and expected improvements.

cycle2.result: Minimum body of information recorded in 95–100% of records; documentation within 24 hours in all but one applicable record.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.612.other_findings: Prognostic information was not consistently discussed.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11730.topic: Smoking cessation and nicotine replacement on admission
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11730.setting: Four older adult psychiatric inpatient wards (Lancashire and South Cumbria Foundation Trust)
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11730.standard: Trust Smoke-Free standards: smoking status documented on admission; tobacco dependence treatment within 30 minutes; regular MDT review; referral to Tobacco Dependency Team within 24 hours

cycle1.result: Smoking status documented 31% (16/53); treatment within 30 minutes 0%; 83% of smokers eventually prescribed NRT, all >5 hours after admission; MDT review 0%; referral within 24 hours 17%.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11730.other_findings: Only 6 patients had documented tobacco dependence. Re-audit planned after interventions.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afac218.078.setting: Four post-acute rehabilitation hospitals; multi-site retrospective audit

cycle1.result: Mean acute stay 11.8 days, rehabilitation stay 37.6 days; 90.2% (n=333) discharged home; 82.2% (n=256) independently mobile at discharge.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afac218.078.other_findings: Significant between-site differences in acute (median 8–13 days) and rehabilitation length of stay (median 16–39 days).

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znad241.105.setting: Emergency theatre list, tertiary general surgical unit (Oxford University Hospitals)

cycle1.result: Over 18% of patients hypothermic at knife-to-skin.

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znad241.105.intervention: Forced-air warming gowns for 45 minutes preoperatively, through induction and intraoperatively (prospective trial).

cycle2.result: 100% normothermic at knife-to-skin; mean core temperature significantly higher (p=0.012).

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afz183.02.standard: Five standards from NICE (2012) and RCP (2016) stroke guidelines on continence identification and management

cycle1.result: Continence status identified by nursing 100% and medical team 41%; care planning 22%; MDT input 11%; interventions 11%.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afz183.02.intervention: After cycle 1: awareness training and MDT prompt sheet. After cycle 2: individualised assessment within 7 days by the advanced nurse practitioner.

cycle2.result: Cycle 3 showed improvement in all five standards; nursing and medical identification 100% and 91% (abstract truncated).

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afz183.02.other_findings: Cycle 2: medical identification 82%, MDT discussion 100%, continence interventions 66%, care planning fell from 22% to 0%. Three cycles, 66 patients over four months.

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znag087.455.setting: Wirral University Teaching Hospital NHS Trust
DOI:10.1093/bjs/znag087.455.standard: WSES 2020 guidelines: post-operative antibiotic use and duration, intra-operative documentation of severity and contamination, microbiological sampling

cycle1.result: Mean antibiotic duration in complicated appendicitis 9.2 days.

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znag087.455.intervention: Consultant-led education and a revised electronic laparoscopic appendicectomy theatre note with guideline prompts.

cycle2.result: Antibiotic duration in complicated appendicitis fell to 8.4 days.

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znag087.455.other_findings: Variation persisted in prescribing for uncomplicated appendicitis; negative appendicectomy rate 6.5%.

DOI:10.1093/bjd/ljag086.495.topic: Skin cancer surveillance in transplant recipients
DOI:10.1093/bjd/ljag086.495.setting: Tertiary dermatology department, Mater Misericordiae University Hospital, Dublin
DOI:10.1093/bjd/ljag086.495.standard: SUNTRAC and US Delphi consensus guidelines on skin surveillance

cycle1.result: Mean time to first dermatology review 5.76 years post-transplant; medium-risk patients seen at 6.5 years, very high risk within 12 months; 60% had skin cancer.

DOI:10.1093/bjd/ljag086.495.other_findings: Under-35 recipients (mainly thoracic) waited a mean 8.5 years for first review. A QI project is underway.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.450.topic: Urgent GP referrals to mental health services
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.450.setting: Community mental health duty team, Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.450.standard: Trust policy: all urgent GP referrals contacted within 48 hours by the duty team

cycle1.result: Only 13/124 urgent referrals were deemed urgent after telephone assessment; 53 referred to primary care mental health, 24 to secondary CMHT, 20 to older adults, 10 discharged to GP.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.450.other_findings: Recommendations: GP surgery visits to raise awareness and a brief risk assessment to justify urgent referral. Compliance with 48-hour contact was not reported.

DOI:10.1093/bjd/ljag086.357.setting: Contact Dermatitis Unit, University Hospitals of Leicester

cycle1.result: 65 (26.7%) self-reported nickel allergy; 49 (20.2%) patch test positive; sensitivity 63.3%, specificity 82.4%.

DOI:10.1136/emermed-2019-208935.setting: Emergency department, Australian Major Trauma Centre; prospective interventional cohort with online airway registry

cycle1.result: First-attempt success rate 88.5%; hypoxia 8.3%; hypotension 8.3%; any complication 27.4%.

DOI:10.1136/emermed-2019-208935.intervention: Bundle of monthly audit, monthly airway management education and an airway management checklist.

cycle2.result: First-attempt success rate 94.6% (RR 1.07, 95% CI 1.00 to 1.14, p=0.014); hypoxia 8.9%; hypotension 7.0%; any complication 23.6%.

DOI:10.1136/emermed-2019-208935.other_findings: Success rose by 13.4% (p=0.006) in the first month with a monthly trend increase of 1.71% (p<0.001); adverse event rates did not change significantly.

DOI:10.1111/anae.15856.setting: All UK hospitals offering anaesthetic services; 7th National Audit Project (NAP7) of the Royal College of Anaesthetists

cycle1.result: not reported

DOI:10.1111/anae.15856.other_findings: Methods paper describing baseline surveys, a 4-day activity survey and a 1-year case registry of peri-operative cardiac arrest.

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znae271.298.standard: RCS England recommendation (following NHSBT amber alert): tranexamic acid for all adult surgical patients where more than 500 ml blood loss is likely

cycle1.result: not reported

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znae271.298.intervention: Prompt for TXA added to the WHO timeout pre-operative checklist.

cycle2.result: The prompt did not increase the likelihood of a pre-operative TXA dose; change in haemoglobin and transfusion rates were similar between groups.

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znae271.298.other_findings: Numerical TXA administration rates were not given in the abstract.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afaf318.095.setting: Pathfinder service (National Ambulance Service and University Limerick Hospital Group), patients who fell at home without admission
DOI:10.1093/ageing/afaf318.095.standard: 2022 World Guidelines for falls prevention and management; target 100% documentation of eight key assessments

cycle1.result: Falls risk stratification 12.5%; other domains not given individually.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afaf318.095.intervention: Eight practice changes aligned with the World Falls Guidelines (delirium screen, lying/standing BP, ECG, standardised balance and gait, ADL and environmental assessments, risk stratification, 3 key questions).

cycle2.result: Implementation increased by 34% to 71% on average; 3 key questions increased by 72%; falls risk stratification 79%; standardised mobility assessment compliance doubled.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afaf318.095.other_findings: Further improvements being embedded in team education and patient information.

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znab117.102.setting: Department of Plastic Surgery, major trauma centre (St Mary's Hospital, Imperial College NHS Trust)
DOI:10.1093/bjs/znab117.102.standard: Royal College of Surgeons guidance on timely, accurate and accessible operation notes

cycle1.result: 56% of operation notes accessible to nursing staff on the electronic medical record.

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znab117.102.intervention: Bespoke online pop-up reminder to upload operation notes to the electronic medical record.

cycle2.result: 83% of operation notes accessible to nursing staff (p<0.05).

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znab117.102.other_findings: Accessibility was not correlated with case type, surgeon grade or number of surgeons; performance remained below the expected standard.

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znad348.184.setting: General surgery, Birmingham Heartlands Hospital (NHS Trust in West Midlands)
DOI:10.1093/bjs/znad348.184.standard: GIRFT and RCS England recommendations for documentation of laparoscopic cholecystectomy

cycle1.result: Indication, consent, WHO checklist and surgeon details documented in all cases. Omissions: pneumoperitoneum technique 19%, intraoperative drugs 54%, intra-abdominal pressure 95%, number of clips 66%, retrieval method/port 38%, port removal under vision 32%, haemostasis 12%, fascial closure 26%, critical view of safety 49%, anaesthetist names 62%, first surgeon signature 41%.

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znad348.184.intervention: Planned: teaching presentations and an electronic documentation template.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afac218.196.setting: Square Medical Practice, Dundalk (primary care) with secondary care correspondence
DOI:10.1093/ageing/afac218.196.standard: Secondary care letters state indication and duration of DAPT; stop date on prescription; DAPT for correct duration

cycle1.result: 12% of secondary care letters did not specify duration; 43% had no stop date on prescription; 19% on DAPT for incorrect duration; 15% serious medication error.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afac218.196.intervention: Clinical system warnings for DAPT time limits, switching of less appropriate PPIs and reminders to secondary care colleagues.
DOI:10.1093/ageing/afac218.196.other_findings: 14.8% were not prescribed a PPI and 4.9% were admitted with GI bleeding; 24.7% were on omeprazole/esomeprazole with clopidogrel.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afaf318.130.setting: Advanced Nurse Practitioner-led frailty outreach clinic (HSE ICPOP, Sligo)

cycle1.result: 30 patients (31.5%) re-presented to the emergency department after initial assessment.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afaf318.130.other_findings: Cognitive impairment and polypharmacy were the most frequent referral concerns.

DOI:10.1302/1358-992x.2024.14.009.topic: Suspected cauda equina syndrome MRI pathway
DOI:10.1302/1358-992x.2024.14.009.setting: Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board West (Ysbyty Gwynedd)
DOI:10.1302/1358-992x.2024.14.009.standard: SBNS/BASS guidelines for urgent MRI in suspected cauda equina syndrome

cycle1.result: 99% scanned in compliance with SBNS/BASS standards; CES found on imaging in 18%.

DOI:10.1302/1358-992x.2024.14.009.other_findings: 33% of scans were out of hours and 4% had repeat scans within 6 months; referrals rose from 2.5 to 3.5 per week during the COVID-19 peak.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10620.setting: North Kirklees Community Mental Health Team, Older people services (South West Yorkshire Partnership NHS Foundation Trust)
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10620.standard: SWYPFT Trust standards, NICE guidelines and Maudsley Prescribing Guidelines (14th edition); target 100% prolactin monitoring

cycle1.result: Prolactin monitored in 41%.

cycle2.result: Prolactin monitored in 22/43 (51%): first-time users 5/15, long-acting injection 6/8, oral 11/20.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10620.other_findings: 78 patients on antipsychotics; 35 on drugs not needing monitoring. No intervention between audits was described.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10327.topic: Physical health monitoring in severe mental illness
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10327.standard: National and local guidelines on routine physical health monitoring; target 100% compliance within 8 weeks

cycle1.result: Baseline: 140 outstanding blood test results and 16 pending ECG results.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10327.intervention: PDSA cycles: staff training on Kardia ECG interpretation; weekly logging and mop-up of outstanding ECG and blood results; improved cover and swaps during annual leave.

cycle2.result: Outstanding blood results fell to 24 and pending ECGs to 1 in four weeks; 100% compliance by eight weeks.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10327.other_findings: The weekly mop-up was the most effective intervention.

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znad101.191.setting: Prehabilitation service, Nottingham University Hospitals NHS Trust

cycle1.result: Physical activity scores improved significantly in hospital gym (54.4 to 216.7) and community gym (180.5 to 362.0) groups (p<0.001).

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znad101.191.other_findings: Colon surgery patients completing prehabilitation (n=37) had median LoS 5.2 days v 5.6 days for those not in the programme (n=567), p<0.05.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11654.setting: Community mental health teams in Halton, Mersey Care NHS Trust
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11654.standard: NICE-BNF prescription writing guidance and Trust policy on FP10 prescriptions

cycle1.result: Overall compliance 97%; Appendix 3 completion 83%; scanning/documenting FP10s in records 87%; storage and prescription writing 100%.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11654.intervention: Column added to Appendix 3 for NHS numbers and an information/prompt sheet inserted in the FP10 bundle.

cycle2.result: Overall compliance 99%; Appendix 3 completion 100%; documentation in records 97%; storage and prescription writing 100%.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11654.other_findings: The community FP10 management procedure was reviewed and rewritten.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.589.standard: Psychiatric Liaison Accreditation Network (PLAN) standards for documentation of assessments

cycle1.result: Collateral history 23%; past medical history 30%; patient/carer perspective 46%; written correspondence offered to patients 0%.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.589.intervention: Presentation of results to team, emailed instructions to create a PLAN-based assessment template, and lobbying for Cerner access at the liaison office.

cycle2.result: Collateral history 67%; past medical history 70%; patient/carer perspective 74%; written correspondence offered 20%.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.589.other_findings: Staff were positive about writing to patients but cited workload as a barrier.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10591.topic: Smoking cessation and nicotine replacement on admission
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10591.setting: Adult psychiatry inpatient wards, North Wales
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10591.standard: Smoking status documented; NRT within four hours of admission; contraindications documented; drug interactions considered

cycle1.result: Smoking status assessed 79%; NRT within four hours 59%; contraindications and drug interactions considered 14%.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10591.other_findings: Recommendations: clinician training and a standardised NRT tool.

DOI:10.1111/anae.16175.setting: Independent sector hospitals; 7th National Audit Project (NAP7) of the Royal College of Anaesthetists

cycle1.result: 174/442 (39%) independent hospitals participated; preparedness survey response 23 (13%); activity survey (1912 responses) suggested suboptimal compliance with monitoring recommendations; 17 cardiac arrest reports (2% of NAP7).

DOI:10.1111/anae.16175.other_findings: Outcomes were similar to the NHS despite lower-risk case mix; quality of care was less often rated favourable than NHS reports.

DOI:10.1136/gutjnl-2014-307263.194.setting: Royal Blackburn Hospital, district general hospital

cycle1.result: Sustained virological response in 264 (60.41%); 43 (9.84%) non-responders; 49 (11.21%) did not complete treatment.

DOI:10.1136/gutjnl-2014-307263.194.other_findings: Patient feedback on the nurse-led service was very positive.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afac218.181.setting: Hospitals reporting to the Irish National Audit of Stroke (INAS); online survey of audit co-ordinators

cycle1.result: Responses from 11/34 audit co-ordinators (10/24 hospitals); variability in data points chosen for hospital arrival time, team time and brain imaging time.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afac218.181.other_findings: Thrombolysis and thrombolysis time showed less variability in interpretation.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afad156.206.setting: Level four hospital (University Hospital Waterford); medical, surgical and orthopaedic admissions
DOI:10.1093/ageing/afad156.206.standard: Correct and timely prescription and administration of Parkinson's disease medication

cycle1.result: 86% did not receive appropriate PD medication in ED; 21% had prescribing errors on admission; 75% missed at least one levodopa dose (83 missed doses); 64% had doses delayed by more than 1 hour; 18% received antidopaminergic drugs.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afad156.206.intervention: Hospital guideline for managing PD patients who are nil by mouth, approved by the Medications and Therapeutics committee, with education sessions at changeover.
DOI:10.1093/ageing/afad156.206.other_findings: 40% of missed doses were due to nil by mouth and 21% had no reason documented; over 80% of delays were perioperative. Re-audit planned after 6 months.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afaf368.011.setting: Health Care of the Older Person ward, Lincoln County Hospital
DOI:10.1093/ageing/afaf368.011.standard: Structured medication review supported by STOPP/START and Beers criteria for patients ≥65 on ≥5 regular medications

cycle1.result: SMR completed 80%; documentation 80%; PIMs prescribed in 40%; changes communicated to GP via EDD 100%.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afaf368.011.intervention: Staff education sessions, e-mail reminders and ward posters.

cycle2.result: SMR completed 100%; documentation 100%; PIMs prescribed in 70%; changes communicated to GP 100%.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afaf318.048.setting: Geriatric Emergency Medicine Unit, University Hospital Limerick
DOI:10.1093/ageing/afaf318.048.standard: 11-standard audit tool based on the World Guidelines for Falls Prevention and Management (2022) and ESC syncope guidelines (2018)

cycle1.result: Compliance ranged 15-100% across 11 standards; composite compliance 65%; careful history 55%; ECG 60%; lying and standing BP 25%.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afaf318.048.intervention: Team-based education on assessment practices and a 'falls from a standing height checklist'.

cycle2.result: Composite compliance 90%; careful history 100%; ECG 90%; lying and standing BP 65%.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afaf318.048.other_findings: Three cycles: re-audits in Q2 2024 and Q1 2025.

DOI:10.1111/anae.16644.topic: Frailty and survival after emergency laparotomy
DOI:10.1111/anae.16644.setting: National Emergency Laparotomy Audit data linked to ONS mortality

cycle1.result: Beyond 90 days, adjusted hazard ratios versus CFS 1–3: CFS 4 1.52, CFS 5 1.69, CFS 6 2.14, CFS 7 2.97, CFS 8 4.24, CFS 9 3.34.

DOI:10.1111/anae.16644.other_findings: Frailty was strongly associated with death within 90 days and the association persisted afterwards.

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znag087.007.setting: National Emergency Laparotomy Audit; 15 geographic regions
DOI:10.1093/bjs/znag087.007.standard: NELA process standards (critical care admission, CT imaging, data completeness, elderly assessment)

cycle1.result: Mortality fell from 11.36% (2016) to 8.15% (2025); regional mortality ranged 5.4% (London South West) to 11.3% (Yorkshire & Humber).

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znag087.007.other_findings: Critical care admission stable (78% to 77.5%); CT imaging declined (65% to 54%); data capture decreased (91% to 83%).

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afae178.180.setting: Three rehabilitation wards, St Mary's Hospital, Phoenix Park, Dublin
DOI:10.1093/ageing/afae178.180.standard: NICE: VTE risk assessment within 24 hours of admission; HSE VTE Prevention Programme template

cycle1.result: VTE risk assessment on admission 0%; therapeutic anticoagulation continued 23 (56%); appropriate prophylaxis started 3 (7%); 8 eligible at-risk patients had no prophylaxis.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afae178.180.intervention: VTE Prophylaxis Protocol based on the HSE template incorporated into the admission booklet on 3 pilot wards (February 2024).

cycle2.result: VTE risk assessment within 24 hours 10 (40%); anticoagulation continued 9 (36%); appropriate prophylaxis 5 (20%); 3 at-risk patients had no prophylaxis; 1 inappropriately received prophylaxis.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afae178.180.other_findings: No association between prophylaxis prescribing and protocol use was shown in this small sample.

DOI:10.1136/gutjnl-2014-307263.575.setting: West Suffolk Hospital, district general hospital
DOI:10.1136/gutjnl-2014-307263.575.standard: National confidential enquiry into PEG outcomes (patient selection); PEG indication, antibiotic prophylaxis documentation and MDT review

cycle1.result: Antibiotic prophylaxis documented 80%; 7 patients had no MDT discussion; 3 deaths within 30 days.

DOI:10.1136/gutjnl-2014-307263.575.intervention: Multidisciplinary nutrition team approach and PEG referral proforma.

cycle2.result: Antibiotic prophylaxis documented 83%; all patients had MDT discussion; 2 immediate complications; no deaths at 30 days.

DOI:10.1136/gutjnl-2014-307263.575.other_findings: Dysphagia after stroke as indication fell from 56% to 39%.

DOI:10.1177/2051415819873263.topic: Staging bone scans in prostate cancer
DOI:10.1177/2051415819873263.setting: BAUS radical prostatectomy database; UK nationwide audit
DOI:10.1177/2051415819873263.standard: Guidelines to avoid staging bone scans in low-risk prostate cancer

cycle1.result: Proportion of low-risk patients having bone scan fell to less than 1% in 2016; intermediate-risk proportion remained stable; no staging scan before RP 3.66% in 2016.

DOI:10.1177/2051415819873263.other_findings: Data quality improved from 2011 and 13 of 15 regions improved data completeness.

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znae271.200.setting: East Surrey Hospital, single NHS Trust in England
DOI:10.1093/bjs/znae271.200.standard: 2021 ESGAR guidance on management of gallbladder polyps

cycle1.result: 35 (36%) had laparoscopic cholecystectomy, including all with polyp >10mm; histology cholecystitis 69%, true gallbladder polyp 6%; 47% of symptomatic patients had two ultrasounds and two clinic appointments. Adherence to ESGAR was inconsistent.

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znae271.200.other_findings: 74% (26/35) of cholecystectomy patients had biliary symptoms and 77% (20/26) of these had cholecystitis on histology.

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znag063.145.setting: General surgical department (South Tyneside and Sunderland, Royal Marsden, Northumbria and North Tees affiliations)
DOI:10.1093/bjs/znag063.145.standard: European Hernia Society guidelines: perioperative antibiotics only for high-risk hernia repairs

cycle1.result: Perioperative antibiotics given in 87.8% overall: 89% elective groin, 85% elective ventral/umbilical, 80% emergency repairs.

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znag063.145.intervention: Departmental standardised 'high-risk criteria' defining when antibiotics are indicated, with departmental education.
DOI:10.1093/bjs/znag063.145.other_findings: Postoperative complication rates stayed low and did not increase.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.476.setting: Early Intervention for Psychosis team, Mersey Care NHS Foundation Trust
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.476.standard: DVLA guidance: documentation of diagnosis, driving status, vehicle type, advice on effect on driving, restrictions and legal duty to inform DVLA

cycle1.result: Diagnosis documented 95% (38); driving status 67.5% (27); vehicle type 33% (5) of drivers; told condition may affect driving 33% (5); driving restrictions advice 67% (10); legal duty to inform DVLA 47% (7).

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.476.other_findings: Recommendations: training, team meetings, adding driving to structured initial assessments and patient leaflets.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11745.setting: Section 136 suite, Fieldhead Hospital, Wakefield (South West Yorkshire Partnership NHS Foundation Trust)
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11745.standard: Local s136 standard operating procedures: timeliness of MHA assessment, IHBTT involvement, documentation and GP communication

cycle1.result: 60% assessed within four hours and 90% within twelve hours; IHBTT face-to-face input 45%; 99% of assessments documented by Section 12 doctors; over 70% of discharged patients lacked documented GP correspondence.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11745.other_findings: 60% of presentations were out of hours and 55% were known to CMHTs.

DOI:10.1302/1358-992x.2023.4.006.setting: Virtual fracture clinic, University Hospital of Wales, Cardiff (CAVUHB)
DOI:10.1302/1358-992x.2023.4.006.standard: Appropriate VFC referrals, compared with established VFCs in England

cycle1.result: Inappropriate referrals for soft tissue knee and shoulder injuries 15.1% (n=50).

cycle2.result: Average 19% improvement in referral quality; inappropriate soft tissue referrals 4.5% (n=15); fracture clinic appointments rose by 8% to 74.4% (n=247).

DOI:10.1302/1358-992x.2023.4.006.other_findings: 64% (n=27) of radial head fractures were still seen in clinic after VFC referral; the rise in clinic appointments was mainly from nurse practitioner referrals.

DOI:10.1093/bjd/ljag086.101.setting: Tertiary dermatology centre, Newcastle upon Tyne Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: Of 52 tests with results, 11 (21%) found a pathogenic or likely pathogenic variant, 4 (8%) a VUS and 37 (71%) no pathogenic variant.

DOI:10.1093/bjd/ljag086.101.other_findings: Yield was 43% for mosaic skin disorders, 60% for ichthyosis and keratoderma and 0% for familial melanoma.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afad156.082.setting: Four surgical wards, Mater Misericordiae University Hospital, Dublin
DOI:10.1093/ageing/afad156.082.standard: CPOC and BGS guideline for perioperative care for people living with frailty: 4AT delirium screening in surgical inpatients over 65

cycle1.result: Baseline 4AT documented preoperatively 25% (n=9); 4AT documented during admission 33% (n=11).

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afad156.082.intervention: Educational sessions for ward-based medical, nursing and allied health staff.

cycle2.result: Baseline 4AT documented preoperatively 35% (n=19); 4AT documented during admission 47.3% (n=26).

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afad156.082.other_findings: Delirium incidence 14.5% (8 patients with 4AT >4); all patients had ≥2 risk factors.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afaf318.175.setting: Geriatric medicine service, St Vincent's University Hospital, Dublin
DOI:10.1093/ageing/afaf318.175.standard: HIQA National Standard for Discharge Summary Information (2013)

cycle1.result: Clinical course 40%; primary diagnosis 85%; stopped medications 40%; future plans 85%; ideal summaries 20%.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afaf318.175.intervention: NCHD-designed flowchart, targeted education sessions and weekly reports on outstanding summaries to consultants.

cycle2.result: Clinical course 75% (p=0.004); primary diagnosis 100% (p=0.002); stopped medications 70% (p=0.016); future plans 97% (p=0.062); ideal summaries 40% (p=0.104); composite score 0.63 points higher (p=0.022).

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afaf318.175.other_findings: Four cycles over three years, 20 patients each. New or changed medications (85%-75%), complications (80%-85%) and complete discharge medications (57%-60%) did not improve.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afaf318.150.setting: Model 2 hospital (University Hospital Limerick affiliation), inpatients
DOI:10.1093/ageing/afaf318.150.standard: Adapted MediDocQ patient safety instrument for prescribing and transcribing documentation

cycle1.result: As-required prescribing completeness 35%; discontinuation completeness 21%; allergy status documented 90%; nature of reaction documented 43%.

cycle2.result: As-required prescribing completeness 33%; discontinuation completeness 31%; allergy status 100%; nature of reaction 31%.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afaf318.150.other_findings: No convincing or consistent improvement; polypharmacy 76% and hyperpolypharmacy 46%.
